message.content:
The required result follows from the assumption that 'the wall temperature distribution is "θ_w(x)=C/x"'.

Let the temperature excess over the constant ambient temperature be

\[
\theta_w(x)=T_w(x)-T_\infty=\frac{C}{x},
\]

where \(C\) has dimensions of temperature \(\times\) length, \(K\,m\). Assume laminar natural convection along a vertical surface, constant fluid properties, no external forced flow, and a constant ambient temperature. The local Grashof number is

\[
Gr_x=\frac{g\beta \theta_w x^3}{\nu^2}
     =\frac{g\beta C}{\nu^2}x^2 .
\]

For a self-similar laminar natural-convection boundary layer with a wall temperature varying as \(\theta_w\propto x^m\), the usual scalings are

\[
u_{\max}\sim \left(g\beta \theta_w x\right)^{1/2},\qquad
\Delta \sim x\,Gr_x^{-1/4},
\]

\[
v_\infty \sim u_{\max}\frac{\Delta}{x},\qquad
q'' \sim k\frac{\theta_w}{\Delta}.
\]

Here \(m=-1\), so \(\theta_w=C/x\). Substituting gives the following variations with \(x\):

\[
u_{\max}\sim \left(g\beta C\right)^{1/2}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
u_{\max}\propto x^0,
\]

\[
\Delta \sim \frac{x}{Gr_x^{1/4}}
= \frac{x}{\left(g\beta C x^2/\nu^2\right)^{1/4}}
= \nu^{1/2}(g\beta C)^{-1/4}x^{1/2}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\Delta \propto x^{1/2},
\]

\[
v_\infty \sim u_{\max}\frac{\Delta}{x}
\sim \left(g\beta C\right)^{1/2}
      \frac{\nu^{1/2}(g\beta C)^{-1/4}x^{1/2}}{x}
= \nu^{1/2}(g\beta C)^{1/4}x^{-1/2}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
v_\infty \propto x^{-1/2}.
\]

For the local heat flux,

\[
q'' \sim k\frac{\theta_w}{\Delta}
= k\frac{C/x}{\nu^{1/2}(g\beta C)^{-1/4}x^{1/2}}
= k\,C\,(g\beta C)^{1/4}\nu^{-1/2}x^{-3/2}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
q'' \propto x^{-3/2}.
\]

If \(Q(x)\) is the heat-transfer rate per unit width from a finite starting point \(x_0>0\) to location \(x\), then

\[
Q(x)=\int_{x_0}^{x}q''(s)\,ds
\propto x_0^{-1/2}-x^{-1/2}.
\]

Thus the local heat flux decays as \(x^{-3/2}\), the cumulative heat rate approaches a finite value as \(x\to\infty\), and the remaining heat rate beyond \(x\) is proportional to \(x^{-1/2}\).

Numerical constants depend on the exact similarity solution and on the Prandtl number, but the powers of \(x\) are independent of those details:

\[
\boxed{u_{\max}\propto x^0}
\]

\[
\boxed{\Delta\propto x^{1/2}}
\]

\[
\boxed{v_\infty\propto x^{-1/2}}
\]

\[
\boxed{q''\propto x^{-3/2}}
\]

\[
\boxed{Q(x)\text{ has a finite asymptote with a correction }\propto x^{-1/2}}
\]

If by \(v(\infty)\) you mean the velocity in the true far field, then it tends to zero; the \(x^{-1/2}\) scaling above is the normal velocity at the edge of the self-similar boundary layer.

As to physical obtainability: the prescribed distribution \(\theta_w=C/x\) is singular at the leading edge \(x=0\), because \(\theta_w\to\infty\) and \(q''\to\infty\) there. Therefore the flow is not physically realizable if the \(1/x\) temperature law is imposed all the way to the actual leading edge. It can be realized physically only if the leading edge has finite temperature and the \(1/x\) law is valid only downstream of a finite starting point, for example

\[
x\ge x_{\min}>0,
\]

or equivalently by using a shifted finite distribution such as \(\theta_w=C/(x+x_0)\) with \(x_0>0\). Under those conditions, the flow would arise on a vertical surface whose wall temperature is externally maintained or generated in a hyperbolic-decay form, with quiescent ambient fluid, constant properties, and laminar natural convection sufficiently away from the leading edge.
